causal:influence:aadc_activity:positive:.evidence: Swoboda KJ et al., Ann Neurol 2003 (AADC deficiency, OMIM 608643: markedly reduced CSF HVA — the single most sensitive diagnostic marker); Blau N et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (AADC deficiency: CSF HVA and 5-HIAA < 10% of normal); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (dopamine catabolism: CNS dopamine -> HVA via MAO and COMT, reflected in CSF HVA) | intervention: AADC deficiency (DDC gene LoF, OMIM 608643): do(aadc_activity=low) -> csf_hva falls to < 10% of normal
causal:influence:aadc_activity:positive:.mechanism: AADC produces dopamine in dopaminergic CNS neurons; CSF homovanillic acid (HVA) is the principal dopamine catabolite in the CNS, reflecting central dopaminergic turnover; higher AADC activity raises CNS dopamine synthesis and CSF HVA; AADC deficiency dramatically reduces CSF HVA (the key diagnostic criterion for AADC deficiency)

causal:influence:aadc_activity:positive:.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine — AADC deficiency (OMIM 608643): markedly reduced urinary HVA and 5-HIAA (key diagnostic markers); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (dopamine catabolism by MAO/COMT to HVA); Swoboda KJ et al., Ann Neurol 2003 (AADC deficiency: profound reduction of HVA in urine and CSF) | intervention: AADC deficiency (DDC gene LoF, OMIM 608643): do(aadc_activity=low) -> urinary_homovanillic_acid falls dramatically
causal:influence:aadc_activity:positive:.mechanism: AADC produces dopamine from L-DOPA; dopamine is catabolised via MAO and COMT to homovanillic acid (HVA), the principal dopamine end-metabolite; higher AADC activity raises dopamine flux and thereby HVA formation and urinary excretion; AADC deficiency (LoF) dramatically reduces urinary HVA

causal:influence:abca1_activity:positive.evidence: Bodzioch M et al. Nat Genet 1999 (Tangier disease = ABCA1 mutations, HDL and apoA-I deficiency); OMIM 205400 (Tangier disease); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism | intervention: ABCA1 loss-of-function (Tangier disease, OMIM 205400): do(ABCA1 activity down) -> plasma apoA-I severely reduced
causal:influence:abca1_activity:positive.mechanism: ABCA1 mediates cellular cholesterol and phospholipid efflux to lipid-poor apoA-I, forming nascent HDL; without ABCA1-mediated lipidation, apoA-I is rapidly catabolized by the kidney and liver; Tangier disease (ABCA1 LoF, OMIM 205400) causes near-total absence of plasma apoA-I.

causal:influence:activated_protein_C:neg.evidence: Wajima 2009 (APC inactivation of FVa/FVIIIa), BioModels BIOMD0000000340; Nayak 2015 BioModels BIOMD0000000611; Boron & Boulpaep
causal:influence:activated_protein_C:neg.mechanism: APC (with protein S) proteolytically inactivates FVa and FVIIIa, the cofactors of prothrombinase/tenase, reducing thrombin generation

causal:influence:adh:positive:urine_osmo.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-145 (25.2: Physical Characteristics of Urine): 'insufficient pituitary antidiuretic hormone (ADH) release or insufficient numbers of ADH receptors in the collecting ducts means that too few water channels are inserted... Insufficient numbers of water channels (aquaporins) reduce water absorption, resulting in high volumes of very dilute urine.'
causal:influence:adh:positive:urine_osmo.mechanism: ADH (vasopressin) inserts aquaporin-2 water channels into the apical membrane of collecting-duct principal cells, increasing water reabsorption from the tubular lumen; higher ADH concentrates urine (raises urine osmolality), while insufficient ADH release or receptor deficiency yields high volumes of very dilute urine (diabetes insipidus).

causal:influence:adipose_hsl_activity:ne.evidence: Hormone-sensitive lipase deficiency, OMIM:615085 — LoF causes hypertriglyceridaemia due to impaired adipose TG mobilization
causal:influence:adipose_hsl_activity:ne.mechanism: RHEA:12044 (EC 3.1.1.79): a triacylglycerol + H2O = a diacylglycerol + a fatty acid + H(+); triacylglycerol is the substrate; LIPE is rate-limiting for adipose lipolysis

causal:influence:agt_activity:negative:p.evidence: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (AGXT; OMIM 259900): diagnostic signature is elevated urinary oxalate AND glycolate (Scriver's OMMBID — PH1: 'hyperoxaluria with elevated urinary glycolate + oxalate is the diagnostic signature'); elevated plasma glycolate in systemic PH1 | intervention: do(AGT / AGXT loss-of-function)
causal:influence:agt_activity:negative:p.mechanism: In AGT deficiency (PH1), undegraded glyoxylate is reduced by lactate dehydrogenase to glycolate; elevated plasma glycolate is part of the diagnostic signature — reduced AGT activity raises plasma glycolate

causal:influence:agxt2_activity:negative.evidence: OMIM 210100 beta-aminoisobutyric aciduria — autosomal recessive benign trait caused by deficient AGXT2 (hepatic beta-aminoisobutyrate transaminase); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, thymine catabolism (R-BAIB → methylmalonate semialdehyde). | intervention: AGXT2 LoF (beta-aminoisobutyric aciduria, OMIM 210100): AGXT2 activity DOWN → urinary 3-aminoisobutyric acid UP [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:agxt2_activity:negative.mechanism: AGXT2 (alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase 2 / D-3-aminoisobutyrate-pyruvate transaminase) catalyzes the transamination of (R)-3-aminoisobutyrate → methylmalonate semialdehyde, which enters the propionate pathway. AGXT2 LoF (benign beta-aminoisobutyric aciduria) blocks this catabolism so 3-aminoisobutyric acid accumulates in plasma and urine.

causal:influence:alveolar_po2:positive:a.evidence: "Hypoventilation always reduces the alveolar and arterial P 2 except when the subject breathes an enriched O2 mixture." — West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 5
causal:influence:alveolar_po2:positive:a.mechanism: end-capillary/arterial PO2 equilibrates with alveolar PO2; lowering alveolar PO2 lowers arterial PO2

causal:influence:aqueous_humor_outflow_r.evidence: "The level of this pressure is determined mainly by the resistance to outflow of aqueous humor from the anterior chamber into the canal of Schlemm. This outflow resistance results from the meshwork of trabeculae." Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch w16, p. 624
causal:influence:aqueous_humor_outflow_r.mechanism: reduced drainage through trabecular meshwork into canal of Schlemm raises steady-state fluid pressure in anterior chamber

causal:influence:arterial_pco2:positive:.evidence: with a normal PO2, the ventilation increases by about 2 to 3 liters per min for each 1 mm Hg rise in PCO2
causal:influence:arterial_pco2:positive:.mechanism: raised arterial PCO2 -> central (CSF H+) + peripheral chemoreceptor drive -> increased ventilation

causal:influence:arterial_po2:negative:a.evidence: hypoxemia reflexly stimulates ventilation by its action on the carotid and aortic body chemoreceptors
causal:influence:arterial_po2:negative:a.mechanism: falling arterial PO2 -> carotid/aortic body peripheral chemoreceptor discharge -> increased ventilation

causal:influence:bckdh_activity:positive.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray — MSUD (BCKDHA/BCKDHB LoF, OMIM 248600): hypoglycaemia is a documented acute complication; alpha-KIC inhibits PDH (Danner & Doering, J Biol Chem 1977); succinyl-CoA from isoleucine/valine catabolism feeds gluconeogenesis (Lehninger Ch.18). Saudubray (2016) 'Inborn Metabolic Diseases' Ch.21: MSUD metabolic crises include hypoglycaemia. | intervention: MSUD (BCKDH LoF, OMIM 248600): BCKAs accumulate, PDH inhibited, gluconeogenic anaplerosis reduced → plasma glucose falls (hypoglycaemia)
causal:influence:bckdh_activity:positive.mechanism: The BCKDH complex oxidatively decarboxylates branched-chain alpha-keto acids (BCKAs), generating succinyl-CoA (from isoleucine/valine, a gluconeogenic substrate) and acetyl-CoA (from leucine). In MSUD (BCKDH deficiency), accumulating BCKAs — particularly 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoate (alpha-ketoisocaproate) — inhibit pyruvate dehydrogenase and disrupt anaplerosis, impairing hepatic gluconeogenesis and causing hypoglycaemia. do(BCKDH_activity UP) → BCKAs cleared → less PDH inhibition + more succinyl-CoA anaplerosis → hepatic glucose production supported → plasma glucose rises.

causal:influence:beta_galactosidase_acti.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 7 (keratan sulfate catabolism; beta-galactosidase role); Morquio-B / MPS IVB OMIM 253010 | intervention: do(GLB1 activity down) = Morquio-B / MPS IVB (OMIM 253010): urinary keratan sulfate elevated; skeletal dysplasia without neurological involvement [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:beta_galactosidase_acti.mechanism: GLB1 also cleaves beta-galactose from keratan sulfate and lactosylceramide. GLB1 deficiency (Morquio-B / MPS IVB) causes keratan sulfate accumulation — skeletal phenotype without neurodegeneration; enzyme activity inversely predicts keratan sulfate content.

causal:influence:beta_hexosaminidase_b_a.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 21 (beta-hexosaminidase isozymes, Sandhoff disease); Sandhoff disease OMIM 268800; Scriver's Online Metabolic Bases 'GM2 Gangliosidoses' (Gravel et al.): HEXB deficiency causes GM2 and GA2 storage; both neuronal and visceral storage | intervention: do(HEXB activity ↓) = Sandhoff disease (OMIM 268800): GM2 ganglioside and globoside accumulate in brain and viscera
causal:influence:beta_hexosaminidase_b_a.mechanism: HEXB encodes the shared beta-subunit of both HexA (αβ) and HexB (ββ). HEXB deficiency eliminates both isozymes; HexA loss causes GM2 ganglioside accumulation (as in Tay-Sachs), with additional globoside (GA2) storage due to HexB loss — Sandhoff disease

causal:influence:beta_ureidopropionase_a.evidence: Lehninger, Nucleotide metabolism; OMIM 613161 (beta-ureidopropionase deficiency: ureidopropionate accumulates)
causal:influence:beta_ureidopropionase_a.mechanism: UPB1 hydrolyses N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine to beta-alanine; more UPB1 consumes more substrate.

causal:influence:blood_hemoglobin_concen.evidence: "a reduction of capillary blood volume or concentration of hemoglobin by disease can reduce the measured diffusing capacity of the lung" (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 3)
causal:influence:blood_hemoglobin_concen.mechanism: hemoglobin binds CO in the capillary; lower Hb raises the reaction-rate resistance 1/(theta*Vc), lowering measured DLCO

causal:influence:blood_viscosity:positiv.evidence: "The hypertension is exaggerated by the polycythemia, which raises the viscosity of the blood." (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 9)
causal:influence:blood_viscosity:positiv.mechanism: higher blood viscosity increases resistance to flow through the pulmonary circulation, raising pulmonary vascular resistance/pressure

causal:influence:bronchiole_diameter:pos.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-124 (22.2): 'This muscular wall can change the size of the tubing to increase or decrease airflow through the tube'; 'bronchospasms … can inhibit air from entering the lungs.' Intervention: do(salbutamol/albuterol, bronchiole_diameter ↑) → alveolar_ventilation ↑; do(bronchoconstriction/asthma, bronchiole_diameter ↓) → alveolar_ventilation ↓. | intervention: Salbutamol/albuterol (β2 agonist bronchodilator): do(bronchiole_diameter ↑) → alveolar_ventilation ↑; asthma attack: do(bronchiole_diameter ↓) → alveolar_ventilation ↓. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:bronchiole_diameter:pos.mechanism: Bronchiole luminal diameter determines airway resistance (Poiseuille: R ∝ 1/r⁴); larger diameter → lower airway resistance → higher airflow for a given pressure gradient → increased alveolar ventilation. Bronchodilators (β2 agonists, ipratropium) widen bronchioles and improve alveolar ventilation in asthma/COPD. Bronchoconstriction (asthma, histamine) reduces diameter and decreases ventilation.

causal:influence:calcitriol:negative:pth.evidence: Peterson & Riggs 2010; standard endocrinology (vitamin D - PTH feedback)
causal:influence:calcitriol:negative:pth.mechanism: calcitriol directly suppresses PTH gene transcription/secretion (VDR feedback)

causal:influence:cellular_atp_level:nega.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-7.3 (7.3: Oxidation of Pyruvate and the Citric Acid Cycle): 'This step is also regulated by negative feedback from ATP and NADH and a positive effect of ADP.'
causal:influence:cellular_atp_level:nega.mechanism: Allosteric feedback inhibition: high ATP suppresses isocitrate dehydrogenase activity (step 3 of TCA cycle), slowing the cycle when energy is abundant

causal:influence:co2_production:positive.evidence: "CO2 production ... is increased by factors such as exercise, fever, infection, nutritional intake, and seizures and decreased by hypothermia and fasting" combined with the alveolar ventilation equation relating PCO2 to CO2 output (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 2)
causal:influence:co2_production:positive.mechanism: with alveolar ventilation held constant, raising metabolic CO2 production raises arterial PCO2 (alveolar ventilation equation, arterial = alveolar PCO2)

causal:influence:core_temperature:positi.evidence: Stolwijk 1971 vasomotor control; HumMod (core temperature -> skin blood flow) | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-003 (1.4: Functions of Human Life): 'increased body temperature can cause … the dilation of blood vessels in the skin in order to decrease body temperature'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-004 (1.5: Requirements for Human Life): 'The body responds to cold by reducing blood circulation to the extremities... in order to prevent blood from cooling there and so that the body's core can stay warm.'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-005 (1.6: Homeostasis): 'Blood vessels in the skin begin to dilate allowing more blood from the body core to flow to the surface of the skin allowing the heat to radiate into the environment'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-027 (5.4: Functions of the Integumentary System): 'arterioles in the dermis dilate so that excess heat carried by the blood can dissipate through the skin and into the surrounding environment'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-115 (20.6: Circulatory Pathways): 'When the ambient temperature is warm, more blood is diverted to the superficial veins where heat can be more easily dissipated to the environment. In colder weather, there is more constriction of the superficial veins and blood is diverted deeper where the body can retain more of the heat.'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-143 (24.7: Energy and Heat Balance): hypothalamus initiates increasing circulation to surface to allow dissipation of heat through skin when temperature too high; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-33.3 (Homeostasis): 'Vasodilation brings more blood and heat to the body surface, facilitating radiation and evaporative heat loss'; 'Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow in peripheral blood vessels.'
causal:influence:core_temperature:positi.mechanism: warm signal causes active cutaneous vasodilation, increasing skin perfusion

causal:influence:cortisol:negative:il6.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (glucocorticoid receptor represses IL-6 transcription) — primary molecular anchor [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cortisol:negative:il6.mechanism: glucocorticoid receptor represses IL-6 gene transcription (NF-kB transrepression), damping the acute-phase response

causal:influence:cortisol:positive:ldl_c.evidence: "Glucocorticoids have robust effects on multiple aspects of lipid metabolism, inducing expression of HMG-CoA reductase to promote cholesterol synthesis ... hyperlipidemia is commonly seen in the setting of glucocorticoid treatment, and insulin resistance induced by glucocorticoids amplifies the hyperlipidemia." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 41, p. 1587
causal:influence:cortisol:positive:ldl_c.mechanism: Glucocorticoids induce HMG-CoA reductase (↑cholesterol synthesis), increase FASN (↑lipogenesis), decrease LPL (↓TG clearance) → net hyperlipidemia including elevated LDL; insulin resistance amplifies effect

causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.evidence: Dexamethasone/corticosterone raise secreted plasma fibronectin ~2.8-fold in hepatocyte culture, with 6-fold FN1 mRNA induction blocked by transcription inhibitors and abolished by a GR-competing antagonist (GR-mediated). PMID:3611064 (Nimmer et al., 'Regulation of plasma fibronectin biosynthesis by glucocorticoids in chick hepatocyte cultures', J Biol Chem 1987) — verified real.
causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.mechanism: Plasma fibronectin (FN1) is synthesized by hepatocytes. Glucocorticoids acting via the glucocorticoid receptor induce FN1 transcription (~6-fold mRNA rise) and improve secretion efficiency, raising secreted plasma fibronectin ~2.8-fold; GR antagonist abolishes the effect dose-dependently. do(cortisol up) -> hepatic fibronectin synthesis/secretion up -> plasma fibronectin up.

causal:influence:cosmc_chaperone_activit.evidence: Germline C1GALT1C1 mutations cause multisystem chaperonopathy with Tn-antigen accumulation. Ju et al. PMID 18537974 (New mutations in C1GALT1C1 in Tn-positive phenotype). | intervention: do(C1GALT1C1 LoF) — genetic loss-of-function of COSMC chaperone [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cosmc_chaperone_activit.mechanism: COSMC (C1GALT1C1) is the ER chaperone required for T-synthase (C1GALT1) to fold and function; T-synthase extends the Tn-antigen (GalNAc-Ser/Thr) to the Core 1 O-glycan T-antigen. Loss of COSMC (Tn syndrome, somatic or germline C1GALT1C1 mutations) abolishes T-synthase activity, causing Tn-antigen to accumulate on cell-surface glycoproteins.

causal:influence:cpt2_activity:positive:.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Inherited disorders of fatty acid metabolism' — CPT-II deficiency (OMIM 255110): elevated C16/C18 acylcarnitines, hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, hepatomegaly; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, carnitine shuttle mechanism. | intervention: do(CPT2 loss-of-function) — carnitine cycle blocked, LCFA cannot reach mitochondrial matrix
causal:influence:cpt2_activity:positive:.mechanism: CPT2 regenerates long-chain acyl-CoA from acylcarnitine at the inner mitochondrial membrane, completing the carnitine cycle and enabling LCFA entry into the beta-oxidation spiral; CPT-II deficiency blocks LCFA import into the mitochondrial matrix, impairs beta-oxidation and hepatic acetyl-CoA supply, reducing ketogenesis and causing hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.

causal:influence:cyp11b1_activity:negati.evidence: "The condition arises because of mutations in the 11β-hydroxylase (CYP11B1) gene that result in loss of enzyme activity and a block in the conversion of 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol. ... the diagnosis can be made by measuring a plasma synacthen–stimulated 11-deoxycortisol value, which will be greater than 52 nmol/L" Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 15, p 534–535
causal:influence:cyp11b1_activity:negati.mechanism: CYP11B1 (11β-hydroxylase) converts 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol; LoF blocks this conversion, causing 11-deoxycortisol to accumulate

causal:influence:cyp17a1_activity:positi.evidence: "Ketoconazole, an orally active substituted imidazole derivative, suppresses gonadal and adrenal biosynthesis by inhibiting the enzyme CYP17, which regulates both 17-hydroxylation and the scission (17,20-lyase) of 17α-hydroxypregnenolone (Δ5-17P) to DHEA" and "secretion, testosterone secretion, height velocity and rate of bone maturation, and aggressive and hyperactive behavior have reportedly been decreased by treatment with oral medroxyprogesterone acetate" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 26, p 1142–1143
causal:influence:cyp17a1_activity:positi.mechanism: CYP17A1 17,20-lyase catalyses androgen precursor (17-OH-pregnenolone → DHEA) supply for Leydig-cell testosterone biosynthesis; ketoconazole inhibition of CYP17 suppresses testosterone production in testotoxicosis boys

causal:influence:cyp21a2_activity:negati.evidence: 21-hydroxylase deficiency (congenital adrenal hyperplasia), OMIM:201910 — LoF causes progesterone accumulation (mineralocorticoid pathway shunt)
causal:influence:cyp21a2_activity:negati.mechanism: RHEA:50304 (EC 1.14.15.15): progesterone + reduced [NADPH--hemoprotein reductase] + O2 = 21-hydroxyprogesterone + oxidized [NADPH--hemoprotein reductase] + H2O + H(+); progesterone is the substrate

causal:influence:dbh_activity:positive:u.evidence: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology — pheochromocytoma diagnosis by elevated urinary VMA; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine — dopamine-beta-hydroxylase deficiency (OMIM 223360): absent urinary VMA (norepinephrine/epinephrine catabolite); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (catecholamine catabolism: norepinephrine -> normetanephrine -> VMA via MAO + COMT) | intervention: DBH deficiency (DBH gene LoF, OMIM 223360): do(dbh_activity=low) -> urinary_vanillylmandelic_acid falls to zero
causal:influence:dbh_activity:positive:u.mechanism: dopamine beta-hydroxylase produces norepinephrine and (via PNMT) epinephrine; vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) is the terminal urinary catabolite of norepinephrine and epinephrine (via MAO + COMT); DBH deficiency abolishes norepinephrine/epinephrine synthesis, leaving urinary VMA absent; pheochromocytoma with high DBH flux raises urinary VMA (the classic screening test)

causal:influence:dendritic_cell_activati.evidence: OmniPath ligrec IL12A->IL12RB1/IL12RB2 consensus_stimulation=True (refs SIGNOR:12023369; Guide2Pharma); Janeway's Immunobiology 9th ed. | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-42.2 (42.2: Adaptive Immune Response): 'Whether a TH1 or a TH2 immune response develops depends on the specific types of cytokines secreted by cells of the innate immune system' — dendritic cells are the principal innate APCs driving TH1 polarisation. Opened primary confirms IL-12 initiates differentiation of naive CD4 T cells into Th1 cells via selective STAT4 activation (Jacobson et al. 1995, J Exp Med, PMID 7722452 / PMC2191986). NB the YAML-cited SIGNOR:12023369 identifier was not verified
causal:influence:dendritic_cell_activati.mechanism: dendritic-cell IL-12 (IL12A/IL12B heterodimer) -> IL-12 receptor (IL12RB1/IL12RB2) on naive CD4 T cell -> STAT4 -> T-bet -> Th1 differentiation/activation (GO:0035722 IL-12-mediated signaling)

causal:influence:dihydropyrimidinase_act.evidence: Lehninger, Nucleotide metabolism; OMIM 222748 (dihydropyrimidinase deficiency: dihydrouracil/dihydrothymine accumulate)
causal:influence:dihydropyrimidinase_act.mechanism: DPYS hydrolyses 5,6-dihydrouracil; more DPYS consumes more dihydrouracil substrate.

causal:influence:dystrophin_level:negati.evidence: PMID 477220; (Abstract; Increased turnover of muscle contractile proteins in Duchenne muscular dystrophy as assessed by 3-methylhistidine and creatinine excretion (1979)); “expression of the data to allow for differences in muscle mass gives fractional degradation rates 2--3 times higher than in age-matched controls” | Dystrophin LoF (Duchenne) raises myofibrillar protein degradation, the source of 3-methylhistidine (occurs only in actin/myosin, not reutilised), so do(lower dystrophin) raises 3-methylhistidine (sign -). [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:dystrophin_level:negati.mechanism: dystrophin level (sarcolemmal integrity) -> when low, myofibrillar (actin/myosin) protein catabolism rises -> release of non-reutilised 3-methylhistidine -> plasma/urinary 3-methylhistidine concentration

causal:influence:dystrophin_level:negati.evidence: Frontiers Physiology 2023 doi:10.3389/fphys.2023.1183101 (DMD disease mechanism, sarcolemmal leakage); Duchenne muscular dystrophy OMIM 310200; Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (skeletal muscle membrane physiology); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 'Muscular Dystrophies' (absent dystrophin → CK 50–300× ULN, sarcolemmal fragility). | intervention: do(dystrophin_level ↓) — Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy, DMD gene loss-of-function
causal:influence:dystrophin_level:negati.mechanism: Dystrophin anchors the sarcolemma to the cytoskeleton via the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex; loss of dystrophin destabilizes sarcolemmal integrity, causing membrane tears during contraction and markedly increased membrane permeability (quality: dystrophin concentration → disposition: sarcolemmal stability → process: contraction-induced membrane tearing → quality: permeability).

causal:influence:efferent_arteriolar_res.evidence: "Increase in resistance of either the afferent or the efferent arterioles reduces peritubular capillary hydrostatic pressure ... constriction of the efferent arterioles ... lowers peritubular capillary hydrostatic pressure" -- Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch 27 (Urine Formation II) Table 27-2, p 341
causal:influence:efferent_arteriolar_res.mechanism: increased efferent arteriolar resistance -> reduced downstream peritubular capillary hydrostatic pressure -> raised net reabsorptive force -> increased Na/water reabsorption (angiotensin II mechanism; Table 27-2: down RE -> up Pc)

causal:influence:elovl6_activity:positiv.evidence: Ohno et al., J Biol Chem 2010 (ELOVL6 extends C16 to C18, ELOVL6 LoF mice show reduced stearate); Matsuzaka et al., Nat Med 2007 (ELOVL6 knockout prevents insulin resistance with altered C16/C18 ratio); Lehninger, Ch. 21 (C16->C18 elongation). | intervention: ELOVL6 loss-of-function: ELOVL6 LoF -> failure to elongate palmitate (C16:0) to stearate (C18:0) -> reduced plasma octadecanoate (stearate) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:elovl6_activity:positiv.mechanism: ELOVL6 (very long chain fatty acid elongase 6) elongates palmitoyl-CoA (C16:0) to stearoyl-CoA (C18:0) by adding two carbons in the endoplasmic reticulum. ELOVL6 is the principal elongase for C16 saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids. ELOVL6 deficiency reduces stearate (C18:0) and increases palmitate (C16:0).

causal:influence:enteropeptidase_activit.evidence: Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-6.6.3 (Zymogen Activation): 'Once in the duodenum, enteropeptidase activates trypsinogen by removing the 7-10 amino acids trypsinogen activation peptide (TAP) from the N-terminal region... Removal of TAP induces a conformational change, resulting in active trypsin.'
causal:influence:enteropeptidase_activit.mechanism: Enteropeptidase cleaves the trypsinogen activation peptide (TAP) from trypsinogen N-terminus, inducing a conformational change that yields active trypsin in the duodenum.

causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:ce.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.29 (Renal Regulation of Potassium, Calcium, Phosphate, and Magnesium; Integration of Renal Mechanisms for Control of Blood Volume and Extracellular Fluid Volume) §b-Adrenergic Stimulation Increases Cellular Uptake of Potassium: “Increased secretion of catecholamines, especially epinephrine, can cause movement of potassium from the extracellular to the intracellular fluid, mainly by activation of b2-adrenergic receptors”
causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:ce.mechanism: epinephrine activates beta2-adrenergic receptors that stimulate the Na+/K+-ATPase, driving K+ from extracellular into intracellular fluid

causal:influence:erythroferrone:negative.evidence: Arezes et al. 2018, "Erythroferrone inhibits the induction of hepcidin by BMP6" (Blood 132:1473-1477, PMID 30097509) — recombinant ERFE suppresses the hepatic BMP/SMAD pathway; Kautz et al. 2014 (Nat Genet 46:678-684, PMID 24880340). [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:erythroferrone:negative.mechanism: Erythroblast-derived ERFE acts as a BMP ligand trap: it sequesters BMP6 (and the BMP2/6 heterodimer), preventing the ligand from binding the hepatocyte BMP type-I receptor ALK3 (disposition), which lowers SMAD1/5/8 phosphorylation and hepatic BMP-SMAD signaling activity.

causal:influence:estradiol:negative:gnrh.evidence: "both testosterone and estradiol (derived from aromatization of testosterone) exert negative feedback effects at the hypothalamus to suppress pulsatile GnRH secretion." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 19, p 683
causal:influence:estradiol:negative:gnrh.mechanism: estradiol acts via ERα in hypothalamic kisspeptin neurons to suppress GnRH pulse secretion

causal:influence:glycogen_phosphorylase_.evidence: Glycogen storage disease type VI / Hers disease (OMIM 232700; PYGL deficiency): fasting hypoglycemia from impaired hepatic glycogenolysis is the cardinal feature, confirming PYGL activity positively drives hepatic_glucose_production. Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 15 (glycogen catabolism: glycogen phosphorylase rate-limits glycogenolysis to G-1-P -> hepatic glucose output). Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray 'Inborn Metabolic Diseases' (GSD VI: hepatic phosphorylase deficiency -> hepatomegaly + fasting hypoglycemia). StatPearls 'Glycogen Storage Disease' (NCBI NBK459277: hepatic GSD types II/III/VI/IX -> fasting hypoglycemia via impaired glycogenolysis). Intervention: do(PYGL LoF, GSD VI, OMIM 232700) -> hepatic glycogenolysis impaired -> hepatic_glucose_production DOWN. | intervention: do(PYGL LoF, Hers disease, GSD VI, OMIM 232700) -> hepatic glycogenolysis blocked -> hepatic glucose production DOWN (fasting hypoglycemia)
causal:influence:glycogen_phosphorylase_.mechanism: Hepatic glycogen phosphorylase (PYGL) catalyzes phosphorolysis of alpha-1,4-glucosidic bonds in liver glycogen, releasing glucose-1-phosphate for conversion to free glucose. PYGL activity is therefore a positive determinant of hepatic glucose production via the glycogenolytic arm. In GSD VI (Hers disease, OMIM 232700), PYGL deficiency impairs hepatic glycogenolysis -> reduced hepatic glucose production -> fasting hypoglycemia (especially post-prandial fasting). PYGL activity UP -> glycogenolysis UP -> hepatic_glucose_production UP.

In urea-cycle disorders (OTC/CPS1/ASS1/ASL/ARG1 deficiency), reduced hepatic urea synthesis lowers BUN despite severe hyperammonemia — the classic 'low BUN with high ammonia' signature of UCDs. Interventionally: do(urea_cycle_enzyme deficiency) -> hepatic_urea_synthesis DOWN -> BUN DOWN.

ApoE-deficient mice show markedly elevated VLDL and IDL; APOE2/2 homozygotes (type III hyperlipoproteinemia / familial dysbetalipoproteinemia, OMIM 617347) have elevated plasma triglycerides due to impaired remnant clearance.

causal:influence:mean_arterial_pressure:.mechanism: rising arterial pressure stretches the carotid-sinus / aortic-arch vessel wall; mechanosensitive baroreceptor disposition -> increased afferent action-potential firing carried via glossopharyngeal/vagal afferents to the NTS.

causal:influence:mean_arterial_pressure:.evidence: Guyton & Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology 13th ed Ch. 21 (Coronary Circulation): coronary blood flow is proportional to aortic diastolic pressure; severe hypotension leads to coronary ischaemia confirming positive pressure-flow relationship. causal:influence:mean_arterial_pressure:.mechanism: Coronary perfusion pressure = mean aortic pressure − right atrial pressure (≈ MAP); coronary blood flow is primarily governed by perfusion pressure during diastole (when left coronary resistance is lowest). Raising MAP increases the driving pressure and, in the absence of compensatory vasoconstriction, raises coronary flow.

MMUT deficiency causes methylmalonic acidemia (MMA): methylmalonate and methylmalonyl-CoA accumulate and directly inhibit succinate dehydrogenase (respiratory complex II), as well as the alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex, impairing the TCA cycle and electron transport chain activity. Secondary mitochondrial dysfunction is a key contributor to the renal and neurological damage in MMA.

causal:influence:otc_activity:negative:c.evidence: OTC deficiency OMIM 311250; urea cycle disorders GeneReviews NBK1217; glutamine elevated in plasma AND CNS in proximal urea cycle disorders; spf-j OTC mouse model shows cerebral glutamine perturbations (PMC4315515); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (glutamine as the non-toxic ammonia carrier in CNS). | intervention: do(OTC loss-of-function) — OTC deficiency OMIM 311250
causal:influence:otc_activity:negative:c.mechanism: OTC deficiency causes hyperammonemia. causal:influence:pah_activity:positive:p.evidence: Phenylketonuria (PAH; OMIM 261600); Scriver et al., OMMBID (PKU chapter): 'tyrosine, the precursor of melanin and catecholamines, is often low without appropriate dietary management'; NBK535378 (StatPearls PKU): 'deficiency of downstream products including catecholamine neurotransmitters'; PMC3470696 (ENU2 mice): 'impaired cortical dopamine synthesis due to reduced tyrosine precursor availability'; Blau et al., Physicians Guide to the Diagnosis, Treatment, and Follow-Up of Inherited Metabolic Diseases. Intervention: do(PAH loss-of-function, phenylketonuria, OMIM 261600). | intervention: genetic LoF of PAH (phenylalanine-4-hydroxylase; phenylketonuria / PKU, OMIM 261600)
causal:influence:pah_activity:positive:p.mechanism: Phenylalanine-4-hydroxylase (PAH) converts phenylalanine to tyrosine, which is the direct precursor for the catecholamine biosynthetic pathway (tyrosine -> DOPA -> dopamine -> norepinephrine -> epinephrine). PAH deficiency (phenylketonuria, OMIM 261600) causes phenylalanine accumulation and simultaneously reduces tyrosine availability. Reduced tyrosine substrate lowers the rate-limiting step of catecholamine synthesis (tyrosine hydroxylase), reducing production of dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine. Do(PAH LoF) -> less tyrosine -> less catecholamine synthesis -> plasma catecholamines fall. PAH active -> sufficient tyrosine -> normal catecholamine production.

causal:influence:plasma_ceruloplasmin:po.evidence: OMIM 604290 (aceruloplasminemia; CP LoF; hallmarks: absent serum ceruloplasmin ferroxidase activity, low serum iron, low transferrin saturation, high ferritin, tissue iron overload); Miyajima et al. 1987 / Yoshida et al. 1995 (aceruloplasminemia: low serum iron with brain and visceral iron accumulation); PMC6290325 (aceruloplasminemia review: absent Cp ferroxidase -> impaired iron export from cells, low transferrin saturation); PMC4050113 (ceruloplasmin-ferroportin system of iron traffic: Cp ferroxidase required for Fe3+ loading onto transferrin); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (ceruloplasmin as ferroxidase: Fe2+ -> Fe3+ for transferrin loading). | intervention: aceruloplasminemia (CP loss-of-function, autosomal-recessive, OMIM 604290) | intervention: aceruloplasminemia (CP/ceruloplasmin loss-of-function, OMIM 604290) [citations PubMed-verified]

Intervention: do(CP LoF / aceruloplasminemia) -> absent ceruloplasmin ferroxidase activity -> failure to load Fe3+ onto transferrin -> low plasma (transferrin-bound) iron.

In Refsum disease (PHYH deficiency, OMIM 266500), phytanic acid is not degraded and accumulates to high concentrations in plasma, where it circulates in all major lipoprotein fractions (VLDL, LDL, HDL). The elevated phytanic acid directly and additively raises total plasma lipid concentration, as phytanic acid is itself a lipid component of plasma.

causal:influence:plasma_sah:negative:hep.evidence: Adenosylhomocysteinase deficiency / AHCY deficiency OMIM 180960; Stender S et al., N Engl J Med 2017 / Buist NRM et al., Am J Hum Genet 2006 (AHCY deficiency causes hepatic dysfunction including hypoalbuminemia); Clarke S & Banfield K, in: Carethers JM ed., OMMBID (SAH as a potent methyltransferase inhibitor, Ki competitive with SAM); Finkelstein JD, J Nutr Biochem 1990 (SAH inhibition of transmethylation reactions); Fowler B, Eur J Pediatr 1998 (clinical spectrum of AHCY deficiency: liver failure, hypoalbuminemia). | intervention: do(AHCY/SAH hydrolase loss-of-function) — adenosylhomocysteinase deficiency OMIM 180960

Accumulation of SAH (as occurs in AHCY/SAH hydrolase deficiency) inhibits DNA methyltransferases and histone methyltransferases in hepatocytes, impairing transcriptional regulation of liver-specific genes including the albumin (ALB) gene. Clinical consequence: AHCY deficiency causes progressive liver disease including hypoalbuminemia. do(AHCY LoF) → SAH ↑ → global methyltransferase inhibition in hepatocytes → reduced albumin gene transcription → hepatic albumin synthesis ↓.

causal:influence:plasma_vitamin_k:negati.evidence: Pharmacological do: warfarin (vitamin K antagonist, blocks VKORC1) raises plasma PIVKA-II; vitamin K supplementation reverses PIVKA-II elevation in neonates and anticoagulated patients — PMID 22280352 (PIVKA-II as marker of subclinical vitamin K deficiency in term infants); PMID 2381266 (PIVKA-II and coagulation factors in warfarin-treated patients); PMID 3735800 (liver and plasma PIVKA-II in vitamin K deficiency in rats). Inborn error corroboration: VKCFD1 (GGCX biallelic mutations) → PIVKA-II accumulation, PMC2643352. Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors). | intervention: Pharmacological: warfarin do(plasma_vitamin_k effective ↓) → plasma_pivka_ii ↑, confirming sign '-'. Also: dietary vitamin K restriction or neonatal deficiency → PIVKA-II rises; vitamin K repletion → PIVKA-II falls. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:plasma_vitamin_k:negati.mechanism: Vitamin K is the obligatory cofactor and electron-donor substrate for the hepatic endoplasmic-reticulum enzyme gamma-glutamyl carboxylase (GGCX), which gamma-carboxylates glutamate residues on prothrombin (and factors VII, IX, X, protein C/S). When plasma vitamin K is sufficient, GGCX fully carboxylates prothrombin to its functional form; when vitamin K is low or pharmacologically blocked (warfarin inhibits the vitamin K epoxide reductase VKORC1, depleting reduced vitamin K), GGCX substrate is absent, carboxylation stalls, and under-carboxylated prothrombin (PIVKA-II / des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin) accumulates in plasma. Raising plasma vitamin K → restores GGCX activity → PIVKA-II falls.

causal:influence:plasma_vitamin_k:positi.evidence: "Warfarin causes this effect by competing with vitamin K for reactive sites in the enzymatic processes for formation of prothrombin and the other three clotting factors, thereby blocking the action of vitamin K" — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch 36 (Hemostasis)
causal:influence:plasma_vitamin_k:positi.mechanism: vitamin K is the obligate cofactor for gamma-glutamyl carboxylase (GGCX) carboxylating clotting factors; warfarin (coumarin) antagonizes the vitamin-K axis, lowering carboxylase output — so raising vitamin K raises GGCX activity

Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab 2000;278(5):E769-77. PMID:10780931 (VERIFIED via PubMed, title/journal/year/pages confirmed). In primary brown adipocytes the sensitivity of UCP1 mRNA to norepinephrine is potentiated by the presence of T3, and the UCP1 promoter responds ~4-fold to cAMP alone, ~4-fold to T3 alone, but ~12-fold to both combined -- a supra-additive (multiplicative) cross-term between the adrenergic (cAMP) and T3 inputs, i.e. a genuine change in the slope of the adrenergic effect with T3. This scales the gain of the existing positive sympathetic_tone -> metabolic_rate edge (its thermogenic component); d(gain)/d(T3) > 0 and the gain stays positive.
